note: MLP64 + softmax aggregation + classifier, the PS-side stages 3-4. This is the only same-board CPU measurement in the project, and it covers one small layer, not the attention engine.
PL is faster than the A9 at the raw arithmetic by 1.45x.
5.01x slower than pure CPU once the CPU<->PL round trip is counted. This is why stages 3-4 were kept on the A9 and only the attention engine went into the PL.

Scalar C interpreter of the SAME instruction stream (instr.mem) over the same 8192-word scratch, -O2, no NEON (the A9 on this part has VFPv3-D16 only), D-cache on. Bit-exact: 22/22 checked blocks (hre, he, q/k/v/z0 and zp for all four modalities) match exp_*.mem. Median of 5 runs; min 7.452, max 7.473. Measured at 2026-10-29 15:25, CPU 650 MHz (XTime = 325 MHz).

20.790 / 7.470 = 2.78x in favour of the CORTEX-A9, not the PL: on the same silicon, over the same instruction stream and the same data, the scalar C interpreter finishes modules 1+2 in 7.470 ms and the PL needs 20.790 ms. The PL does the same work in 2.33x fewer cycles (2,079,001 vs about 4.85M) but is clocked 6.5x lower (100 vs 650 MHz), which more than cancels it. Neither number includes the AXI load or readback. A hand-written int8 dot product would WIDEN this gap, so treat 2.78x as a floor for the A9's lead. Pipelining the accumulator to close 200 MHz gives 10.40 ms, still 1.39x behind.
